messages:
ella_support: FYI support ticket from ACME—EU users reporting big latency spikes and intermittent 401s. Customer claim: requests are landing in us-west despite EU geoip. Can someone triage? ticket: https://acme.jira/RED-4321

lucas_cs: Thanks, can we get a sample request + response headers and the client IP? Also which CDN/resolver they're using?

ella_support: Pasting redacted headers from one customer session:
```
GET /v1/generate HTTP/1.1
Host: api.redwood.example
X-Forwarded-For: 93.184.216.34
X-Client-IP: 93.184.216.34
Authorization: Bearer redacted
X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2
X-Request-Id: rwd-abc-123
```
They included `X-Redwood-Region: us-west-2` in our logs even though they're EU.

rina_neteng: If X-Redwood-Region is set server-side it means our routing picked us-west. Two likely culprits: upstream resolver EDNS client subnet (ISP pushing to us resolver) or stale GeoIP DB on the edge. Can we reproduce from their IP?

marco_sre: I probed from a couple EU endpoints and saw normal EU routing, but I can try a targeted DNS probe from 93.184.216.34's ASN if we have a probe node nearby. In the meantime, run a dig via common public resolvers to see answer differences. Example dig I asked them to run:
```
# from customer network
dig @1.1.1.1 api.redwood.example +short
dig @8.8.8.8 api.redwood.example +short
dig @resolver.local api.redwood.example +short +noedns
```

ella_support: Customer ran those and returned IPs for us-west from 1.1.1.1 and their ISP resolver, but 8.8.8.8 returned eu-pop IP. They also pasted `dig +short` outputs.

dns-bot: note: detected EDNS-Client-Subnet present in resolver responses for 93.184.216.0/24. Records show different A answers between 8.8.8.8 and 1.1.1.1 for that prefix.

lucas_cs: So it's an ECS/ISP resolver issue, not our origin. Is the fallback policy doing automatic region downgrade when health checks fail? That could explain the 401s if the auth token validation is region-specific.

marco_sre: Correct—our regional routing policy falls back to any available variant when capacity/health indicates, and that can set the `X-Redwood-Region` header to the variant region. If a client's token is restricted by region, auth can 401. In this case, seems their ISP resolver returns us-west for them due to ECS mapping to an IP that maps to our US cluster. We should avoid silent cross-region fallback for requests authenticated with region-scoped keys.

rina_neteng: Short remediation steps: 1) ask CS to confirm token scope and tell them to switch to a global token temporarily; 2) add a safety check in routing: if request contains region-scoped auth, do not auto-fallback to a different region—return 503 or route to a compatible region only. 3) Add DNS monitoring to alert when EU client prefixes see non-EU answers.

ella_support: I'll relay the temporary workaround to the customer (global token). Can someone open a follow-up to change fallback behavior?

incident-bot: INCIDENT CREATED: INC-2026-78 - "ECS/ISP-driven DNS answers causing EU->US routing and auth failures" (sev3).

marco_sre: I'll own the routing change. Plan: add region-auth compatibility check to the routing decision tree, and create an allowlist for regex tokens that should never be auto-failed over. Also deploying a small DNS probe fleet to sample EU ISP resolvers (edge-probe) and alert when answer set deviates from canonical EU pool.

rina_neteng: For near-term visibility, ops: can we add an analytic to Console showing percent of requests from EU IPs that hit US clusters by day? That will help quantify the impact and detect ISP-induced drift.

ops-bot: ANNOTATION: dashboard request created - ID dash-geo-787.

lucas_cs: Customer confirmed temporary global token fixed 401s; latency still a bit higher but acceptable. CS to keep them posted.

ella_support: Thanks all — action items: marco to PR routing change, rina to schedule DNS probe rollout, ops to create dashboard, CS to follow up with customer. Marking this thread resolved for support. :thumbsup:
